content: 1. Counseling should be provided to individuals who have received a negative result from an early HIV test to guide them on measures to prevent seroconversion. 2. Current guidelines for the prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) recommend that virological testing for HIV-exposed infants be conducted within the first two months of life. 3. The numerator for this indicator is the number of HIV-exposed infants born during the reporting period who received a virological HIV test within two months (and within 12 months) of birth. 4. The denominator is the estimated number of HIV-positive women who delivered during the reporting period. 5. For the numerator, data should be collected from program records, such as PMTCT registers and laboratory records. For the denominator, modeling-based estimates, such as Spectrum AIM, should be used. 6. The denominator serves as a proxy measure for the number of infants born to HIV-infected women. The recommended reporting period is 12 months. 7. The numerator should be disaggregated by test result (HIV-positive, HIV-negative, indeterminate, or other) to calculate the percentage of positive results and indeterminate results among HIV-exposed infants who received a virological test. 8. The age of the infant (<2 months, 2–12 months) should also be disaggregated to calculate the proportion of exposed infants receiving virological testing within two months and within 12 months of birth. 9. Infant antiretroviral (ARV) prophylaxis coverage measures the percentage of HIV-exposed infants who initiated ARV prophylaxis at birth. 10. This indicator assesses the delivery of prevention services to HIV-exposed infants immediately after birth. 11. ARV prophylaxis for HIV-exposed infants is critical in reducing the risk of mother-to-child transmission during the immediate postpartum period, as part of Prong 3 of the PMTCT strategy. 12. High coverage of ARV prophylaxis among HIV-exposed infants born in healthcare facilities is essential. 13. When using a program-based denominator, the indicator measures coverage among HIV-exposed infants born in facilities, directly reflecting the program’s ability to meet care standards. 14. The numerator is the number of HIV-exposed infants born within the past 12 months who were started on ARV prophylaxis at birth. 15. The population-based denominator is the number of HIV-positive women who delivered within the past 12 months. 16. The program-based denominator is the number of HIV-positive women who delivered in a facility within the past 12 months. 17. For the numerator, data should be collected from program records, such as PMTCT registers. For the population-based denominator, modeling-based estimates, such as Spectrum AIM, should be used. 18. The population-based denominator serves as a proxy measure for the number of infants born to HIV-infected women. For the program-based denominator, data should be collected from program records, labor, and delivery registers. 19. The recommended reporting period is 12 months. 20. The percentage of HIV-positive pregnant women who received antiretroviral therapy (ART) during pregnancy and/or at labor and delivery measures whether a recommended course of ART has been provided to HIV-positive pregnant women. 21. Providing ART to HIV-positive pregnant women is a critical strategy for preventing vertical transmission of HIV. 22. In the “Treat All” era, all HIV-positive pregnant women should be given a recommended ART regimen as soon as possible after diagnosis, including during labor and delivery. 23. The numerator is the number of HIV-positive pregnant women who delivered during the reporting period and received ART during pregnancy and/or labor and delivery. 24. The population-based denominator is the number of HIV-positive pregnant women who delivered during the reporting period. 25. The program-based denominator is the number of HIV-positive pregnant women who delivered during the reporting period and attended antenatal care (ANC) or had a facility-based delivery. 26. For the numerator and program-based denominator, data should be collected from program records, such as PMTCT registers, ART registers, and labor and delivery registers. 27. For the population-based denominator, modeling-based estimates, such as Spectrum AIM, should be used. 28. The recommended reporting period is 12 months. 29. Disaggregation should include age (<15, 15–19, 20–24, 25+) and pregnant women who inject drugs. 30. The numerator should also be disaggregated by the timing of ART initiation: already on ART at the first ANC visit, newly on ART during pregnancy, newly on ART during labor and delivery, or on a non-recommended ART regimen. 31. ART coverage in breastfeeding mothers measures the percentage of HIV-exposed breastfeeding infants whose mothers are receiving ART at 12 (and 24) months postpartum. 32. This indicator assesses the program’s ability to reduce the risk of HIV transmission via breastfeeding (Prong 3). 33. In many countries, the average breastfeeding period is 18–24 months, representing a significant risk period for HIV-exposed infants. 34. Ensuring that HIV-positive mothers remain on ART during the breastfeeding period is critical for sustaining maternal health and preventing infant infection. 35. The numerator is the number of HIV-exposed breastfeeding infants whose mothers are receiving ART at 12 months (and 24 months) postpartum. 36. The denominator is the number of HIV-exposed infants attending maternal and child health (MCH) services for a 12-month visit (and 24-month visit or first visit after the end of breastfeeding). 37. For the numerator, data should be collected from program records, such as PMTCT registers and ART registers. For the denominator, data should be collected from program records, such as MCH service records. 38. Disaggregation should include age (<15, 15–19, 20–24, 25+) and timing of ART initiation (already on ART at the first ANC visit, newly on ART during pregnancy or labor and delivery). 39. The final outcome of PMTCT measures the percentage of HIV-exposed infants whose final outcome status is known. 40. This indicator assesses the quality of program follow-up to track exposed infants and ascertain their final status. 41. Effective PMTCT programs must follow HIV-exposed infants until the end of the breastfeeding period to ensure the full cascade of services and support is provided to HIV-positive mothers and their infants. 42. The numerator is the number of HIV-exposed infants born within the past 12 months (or 24 months in breastfeeding settings) with known final outcome status. 43. The population-based denominator is the estimated number of HIV-positive women who delivered within the past 12 months (or 24 months in breastfeeding settings). 44. The program-based denominator is the number of HIV-exposed infants born within the 12 months (or 24 months in breastfeeding settings) prior to the reporting period and registered in the birth cohort. 45. For the numerator and program-based denominator, data should be collected through cohort birth tracking. For the population-based denominator, modeling-based estimates, such as Spectrum AIM, should be used. 46. Disaggregation of the numerator should include outcome status (HIV-positive, HIV-negative, no longer breastfeeding). 47. Syphilis screening coverage in ANC measures the percentage of antenatal care attendees tested for syphilis. 48. This indicator assesses the extent of routine syphilis screening among pregnant women at their first visit (ideally) or at any antenatal care visit. 49. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in pregnant women, including active syphilis, can cause serious morbidity and mortality among exposed newborns. 50. Routine screening of pregnant women attending antenatal clinics is a cost-effective way to prevent congenital syphilis. 51. The numerator is the number of women attending ANC services during the reporting period who were tested for syphilis. 52. The denominator is the number of women attending ANC services during the reporting period. 53. For the numerator and denominator, data should be collected from program records, such as ANC registers. 54. The recommended reporting period is 12 months. 55. Disaggregation should include age (<15, 15–19, 20–24, 25+). 56. The numerator should also be disaggregated by the visit of testing (first ANC visit, other than the first ANC visit during the current pregnancy) to calculate the percentage of syphilis tests conducted during the first ANC visit among those tested. 57. Syphilis treatment coverage in ANC measures the percentage of antenatal care attendees testing seropositive for syphilis who are treated. 58. This indicator assesses the coverage of treatment for syphilis seropositive ANC attendees. 59. Programs must ensure that pregnant women diagnosed with active syphilis receive effective treatment with the recommended regimen of benzathine penicillin to prevent congenital syphilis. 60. The numerator is the number of syphilis seropositive ANC attendees treated with benzathine penicillin. 61. The denominator is the number of syphilis seropositive ANC attendees within the past 12 months. 62. For the numerator and denominator, data should be collected from program records, such as ANC registers. 63. Disaggregation should include age (<15, 15–19, 20–24, 25+). 64. The percentage of women living with HIV who have been screened for cervical cancer measures the program’s ability to offer and provide cervical cancer screening for women living with HIV. 65. Women living with HIV are more vulnerable than HIV-negative women to developing invasive cervical cancer, which is an AIDS-defining condition. 66. Screening and treatment of precancerous cervical lesions can reduce mortality from cervical cancer by 70%. 67. The numerator is the number of survey respondents who report ever having a screening test for cervical cancer using any of the following methods: visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), Pap smear, or HPV test. 68. The denominator is the number of survey respondents. 69. For the numerator and denominator, data should be collected through representative surveys of women living with HIV. 70. Disaggregation should include age (<15, 15–24, 25–29, 30–49, 50+) and test result (positive, negative, indeterminate, other). 71. The percentage of key population members who avoid healthcare because of stigma and discrimination measures the extent to which perceived stigma and discrimination in healthcare settings result in members of key populations avoiding healthcare. 72. Healthcare settings are one of the most common places where members of key populations experience discrimination. 73. Tracking the proportion of key populations that avoid healthcare due to stigma and discrimination provides managers with information about where to focus efforts to reduce discrimination and perceived discrimination by service providers, as well as identifying areas where service utilization by key populations can be improved. 74. The numerator is the number of survey respondents who answer “yes” to any of the following: “Have you ever avoided seeking… A. any healthcare, B. HIV testing, C. HIV medical care, or D. HIV treatment in the last 12 months… due to any of the following: 1. fear of or concern about stigma, 2. fear or concern that someone may learn you were a [insert KP type], 3. fear of or concern about or experience of violence, 4. fear of or concern about or experiencing harassment or arrest by police?” 75. The denominator is the number of survey respondents. 76. For the numerator and denominator, data should be collected through representative surveys of key populations (e.g., BBS, BSS, HSS+). 77. The recommended measurement periodicity is every 2–3 years. 78. Disaggregation should include age (<25, 25+) and key populations (men who have sex with men, people who inject drugs, sex workers, transgender people).
